explanation: The downstream job consumed handoffs in which every source_weight had been changed to match demand_score rather than preserving the top-level corpus source_weight values. Job 2 appears to preserve and process the received handoffs consistently, so the fault is upstream. The supplied source for job_1 localizes the transformation to select_demand, which writes source_weight from row.get('demand_score', 0) instead of the corpus source_weight field.
cited_evidence: top_level_input corpus has n06-r01 source_weight 5, n06-r02 4, n06-r03 4, n06-r04 4, n06-r05 3, n06-r06 3, n06-r07 3, n06-r08 2.
job_downstream_coverage_priority input needs show source_weight values 9, 8, 7, 6, 6, 5, 4, 3, matching demand_score instead of the top-level corpus source_weight values.
job_downstream_coverage_priority input evidence_sources repeats those incorrect source_weight values, so the corrupted weights were already present in the handoff consumed by job_2.
In generated/protocol_2_2/upstream_demand_provenance.py, select_demand constructs records with "source_weight": row.get('demand_score', 0), directly explaining the observed substitution.
